thread:
lena: Quick smoke for v6.0-int4 on long-context cohort (~7k queries). Topline first, will attach artifacts.
ktang: TL;DR?
lena: p50=50ms, p95=210ms. cost ~=0.39x fp16. global concordance delta = -0.4% (n=7k). long-context slice delta = -2.0% (n=1.6k), CI [-2.6%, -1.4%], p=0.008.
omar: that's past our slice_threshold. which canary policy was used?
canary-bot: Policy lookup: canary.policy.v2 -> slice_threshold=-0.015, global_threshold=-0.008, min_samples=1000, require_pvalue<0.05.
ktang: min_samples met and p<0.05 -> auto-fallback condition satisfied.
lena: digging into traces: hosts serving seq>200 show KV-merge anomalies and the runtime picked int4-kernel-v3 due to a heuristic; older kernel-v2 behaved fine.
omar: kernel mismatch could explain attention drift on long contexts. can you repro locally?
lena: started local microbench (2k seeded long-context). reproduces: delta ~-1.9% same failure mode. swapping kernel->v2 locally reduces delta to -0.3%.
ktang: plan: 1) pause promotion 2) trigger rollback if not already 3) hotfix kernel-selection heuristic to prefer v2 for seq>180 until root cause fixed 4) run stratified A/B with long-context oversample (n=3k).
lena: executing rollback: /rollout rollback --model v6.0-int4 --reason "kernel-selection heuristic caused long-context delta"
canary-bot: Rollout acknowledged. Routing switched to v5.9-fp16 within 90s. Incident INC-2026-0502 created and assigned: lena, ktang. SLA: 72h.
omar: also: propose a safety gate in canary.policy that cross-checks kernel changes vs slice deltas; if new kernel correlates with a failing slice > threshold, auto-fallback and quarantine kernel.
ktang: agree. I'll draft a policy addendum and add a preflight assertion in model-catalog to validate kernel mapping for seqlen ranges.
lena: uploaded artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/1789123456/v6.0-int4-longctx.jsonl. Perf traces at https://redwood.internal/evals/1789123456
omar: scheduling the 3k A/B tomorrow morning, will post microbench diffs and top-50 failing examples here. Thanks all :thumbsup:
